mainTopic: Breaking bread for המוציא: when to break, pieces versus whole loaves, and the special rules for פסח and שבת
overview: This amud is about how to break bread for המוציא. רבא rules that you make the ברכה over the whole loaf first and only then break it, and the הלכה follows him. Next, רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue about pieces and whole loaves: רב הונא says you may bless on a piece, while רבי יוחנן says a whole loaf is best. Everyone agrees that a wheat piece beats a whole barley loaf. רבי ירמיה בר אבא tries to link this argument to a dispute among the תנאים about onions for תרומה, but the גמרא rejects the link: that dispute is about whether a כהן is present and whether the produce will last. A ירא שמים satisfies both views by holding the piece inside the whole loaf, and a ברייתא teaches the same practice. On פסח everyone does this because מצה is 'לחם עני', and on שבת you must break bread over two loaves because of 'לחם משנה'. The amud ends with how the חכמים broke the שבת loaves and with רב אמי and רב אסי making המוציא on the עירוב bread.

steps.title: רבא's Ruling: Bless First, Then Break
steps.stepSummary: After pushing back on רבי חייא, רבא gives his own approach: make the full ברכה on the whole loaf, and only afterward break it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: One makes the blessing, and only afterward breaks the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own ruling in place of רבי חייא's view, which was discussed on the previous amud. He says to finish the ברכה first and only then break the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא held that the ברכה should finish at the same moment the bread is broken. רבא disagrees. He says the ברכה is said over the loaf while it is still whole, and the breaking comes after. The word אֶלָּא signals that רבא is replacing the earlier approach with his own.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: רבא replaces the approach discussed on the previous amud.

phrases.english: One blesses, and afterward he breaks.
phrases.notes: The blessing is said over the loaf while it is still whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier, where רבא challenged רבי חייא. Now רבא gives his own ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make the ברכה over the whole loaf first, then break it.

steps.title: Who Followed Which Practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that the people of נהרדעא followed רבי חייא, while the רבנן followed רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of נהרדעא acted like רבי חייא, and the רבנן acted like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how people actually behaved in practice. Some communities followed רבי חייא and others followed רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The גמרא is recording real-life practice, which shows that both views were actually followed. This sets up the final ruling that comes soon.

phrases.english: The people of Neharde'a acted according to Rabbi Chiyya
phrases.notes: They finished the blessing together with the breaking.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis acted according to Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the two views from the previous step were practiced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both practices existed: נהרדעא followed רבי חייא, and the רבנן followed רבא.

steps.title: רבינא's Family Testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports what his mother told him: his father followed רבי חייא, while the רבנן followed רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: My mother told me, 'Your father acted like רבי חייא,' since רבי חייא said the blessing must finish together with the bread. And the רבנן acted like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a personal report about his own father's practice. It confirms the same split in practice described in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא also restates exactly what רבי חייא held: the ברכה must end together with the breaking of the bread. This makes the two sides very clear just before the final ruling.

phrases.english: Ravina said: My mother told me,
phrases.notes: רבינא's father died when רבינא was young (רש״י), so he learned this from his mother.

phrases.english: your father acted according to Rabbi Chiyya,
as Rabbi Chiyya said:
The blessing must finish together with the bread.
phrases.notes: In other words, the blessing ends exactly as the bread is broken.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis acted according to Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a family testimony that confirms the split in practice from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא's father followed רבי חייא, and the רבנן followed רבא.

steps.title: The הלכה Follows רבא
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling: the הלכה follows רבא. You bless first and then break the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רבא, who said: One blesses, and afterward breaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final decision on the question. The הלכה is like רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though some communities followed רבי חייא, the practical ruling follows רבא. So the ברכה is said over the whole loaf, and only then is the bread broken.
steps.whatToRemember: When making המוציא, finish the ברכה over the whole loaf, and only then break it. This follows רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for how to make המוציא, and people still follow it today.

phrases.english: And the halacha is according to Rava,
who said: one blesses and afterward breaks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the split in practice from steps 2 and 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבא: bless first, then break.

steps.title: רב הונא: Pieces Are Fine
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: if pieces and whole loaves are on the table, רב הונא says you may bless on the pieces, and that covers the whole loaves too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If they brought pieces and whole loaves before them, רב הונא said: One blesses on the pieces, and this covers the whole loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about which bread to bless on. רב הונא says that blessing on the pieces is fine and covers everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִיתְּמַר introduces a dispute between אמוראים. According to רב הונא, a whole loaf has no special priority. One ברכה on the pieces exempts (פוטר) the whole loaves as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: If they brought before them pieces and whole loaves,
Rav Huna said:
One blesses on the pieces
and thereby exempts the whole loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: choosing between a piece and a whole loaf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may bless on the pieces, and that covers the whole loaves.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The Whole Loaf Is Best
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: the best way to do the מצוה is to bless on the whole loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A whole loaf is the best way to do the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposing view to רב הונא. He says the ideal way is to bless on the whole loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב הונא, רבי יוחנן gives a whole loaf priority. The phrase מצוה מן המובחר means the most ideal way to do the מצוה, not the only valid way.

keyTerms.meaning: The choicest, most ideal way to do the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: מצוה מן המובחר does not mean that blessing on a piece is invalid. It only means the whole loaf is the ideal choice.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
A whole loaf is the choicest way of doing the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing side of the dispute with רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally, bless on the whole loaf.

steps.title: Everyone Agrees: A Wheat Piece Beats a Whole Barley Loaf
steps.stepSummary: The dispute only applies when both breads are the same kind of grain. A wheat piece is preferred over a whole barley loaf, according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is a piece of wheat bread and a whole loaf of barley bread, everyone agrees: one blesses on the wheat piece and thereby covers the whole barley loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the dispute. When the piece is wheat and the whole loaf is barley, both רב הונא and רבי יוחנן agree to bless on the wheat piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat is a more important grain than barley. So here, the better quality of the grain outweighs the fact that the barley loaf is whole. The argument about whole versus piece only applies when both breads are made from the same grain.
steps.whatToRemember: Whole versus piece is disputed: רב הונא says a piece is fine, and רבי יוחנן says a whole loaf is best. But a wheat piece beats a whole barley loaf according to everyone.

phrases.english: But if there is a piece of wheat bread
and a whole loaf of barley bread,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַפְּרוּסָה שֶׁל חִטִּין,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that one blesses on the piece of wheat bread,
and thereby exempts the whole barley loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל פְּרוּסָה שֶׁל חִטִּין וּשְׁלֵמָה מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the רב הונא / רבי יוחנן dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wheat piece is preferred over a whole barley loaf, according to all opinions.

steps.title: A Similar Dispute Among the תנאים About Onions for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the dispute matches an argument among תנאים: should תרומה be taken from a whole small onion, or from half of a large onion?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: This is like a dispute among תנאים. One separates תרומה from a whole small onion, but not from half of a large onion. רבי יהודה says: Not so, rather from half of a large onion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא suggests that the bread dispute already existed among the תנאים. He quotes their argument about which onion to use when separating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא prefers a whole small onion, while רבי יהודה prefers half of a large onion. This gives us a source with the same structure as the bread question: whole versus a part of something better. The next step will explain how the two cases line up.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute among תנאים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא כְּתַנָּאֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said: It is like a dispute among Tannaim:
One separates terumah from a whole small onion,
but not from half of a large onion.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא חֲצִי בָּצָל גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: Not so, rather from half of a large onion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the אמוראים' dispute to an earlier dispute among the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread dispute parallels the תנאים' dispute over a whole small onion versus half of a large onion.

steps.title: Spelling Out the Parallel: Important vs. Whole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the onion dispute is about one principle: whether the more important item wins (חשוב עדיף) or the whole item wins (שלם עדיף).
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this: one master holds that the more important item is better, and the other master holds that the whole item is better?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how the onion dispute matches the bread dispute. It names the principle each side holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds חשוב עדיף, so half of a large, better onion wins. The תנא קמא holds שלם עדיף, so the whole small onion wins. If this reading is correct, רבי יוחנן's preference for a whole loaf would match the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (proposes an inference)
The more important item takes precedence

steps.confusionAlert: מאי לאו only proposes a reading. It is not a final conclusion, and the next step rejects this parallel. Also notice which side is which: רבי יהודה = חשוב עדיף, and the תנא קמא = שלם עדיף.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds the more important item takes precedence,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who prefers half of a large onion.

phrases.english: and the other master holds the whole item takes precedence?
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who prefers a whole small onion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the onion source from step 8 matches the bread dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב הונא / רבי יוחנן dispute is the same as the תנאים' dispute about onions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about separating תרומה from onions.

steps.title: The onion dispute is really about whether a priest is present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link between the bread dispute and the onion dispute. When a כהן is present, everyone agrees the more important item wins. The onion argument only happens when no כהן is around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is a priest, everyone agrees that the more important item is better. They only argue where there is no priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the comparison from Step 9. It says the onion dispute is not about 'important vs. whole' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן is present, he can take the תרומה right away. So everyone agrees to give the better item, the half of the large onion. The argument only comes up when there is no כהן, because then the question is which item will last until a כהן arrives. A whole onion keeps, but a cut onion spoils. That is a different issue from our bread case.

keyTerms.meaning: Priest; the one who receives תרומה
Everyone agrees; there is no argument

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the half onion lost because 'whole is better.' The whole small onion is chosen only because it lasts longer when no כהן is there to take it right away.

phrases.english: Where there is a priest,
everyone agrees
phrases.notes: Literally: the whole world does not argue.

phrases.english: that the more important item is preferred.
Where they argue is where there is no priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא כֹּהֵן, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison proposed in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים' onion dispute matches the bread dispute between רב הונא and רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The onion dispute depends on whether a כהן is present and whether the produce will last. It is not about the value of wholeness.

steps.title: A משנה proves the distinction based on whether a כהן is present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that the rule for separating תרומה depends on whether a כהן is present. רבי יהודה says to always use the best.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: wherever there is a priest, one separates תרומה from the best. Wherever there is no priest, one separates from what will last. רבי יהודה says: one separates only from the best.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to back up the rejection in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה openly makes the rule depend on whether a כהן is there. With a כהן present, give the best. Without one, give what keeps. רבי יהודה always prefers the best. So this argument is about lasting quality versus best quality. It is not about whole versus important.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
That which lasts or keeps well

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּהֵן — תּוֹרֵם מִן הַיָּפֶה,
phrases.english: Wherever there is a priest, one separates from the best,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן — תּוֹרֵם מִן הַמִּתְקַיֵּים.
phrases.english: and wherever there is no priest, one separates from what will last.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One separates only from the best.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text that supports the rejection in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the onion dispute depends on whether a כהן is present.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת תרומות distinguishing 'where there is a כהן' from 'where there is no כהן'.
steps.whatToRemember: The onion dispute is about whether the produce will last when no כהן is there. So it cannot settle the bread question.

steps.title: A God-fearing person satisfies both opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says a ירא שמים fulfills both views. מר בריה דרבינא did this by placing the piece inside the whole loaf and breaking them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A God-fearing person fulfills both opinions. Who is this? מר בריה דרבינא, who would put the piece inside the whole loaf and break them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the bread argument. It gives a practical way to satisfy both רב הונא and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no ruling here on who is right. Instead, the person holds both breads together and breaks them. That way the blessing is made on the piece, as רב הונא allows, and also on the whole loaf, as רבי יוחנן prefers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice of holding the piece and the whole loaf together when making the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And a God-fearing person fulfills both.
And who is this? Mar, son of Ravina,
for Mar, son of Ravina,
would place the piece inside the whole loaf and break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the onion comparison and returns to the original bread dispute with a practical solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Place the piece inside the whole loaf and break them together, which satisfies both opinions.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same practice, and שלמן is praised
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited a ברייתא before רב נחמן בר יצחק teaching the same practice. רב נחמן praised him with a pun on his name, שלמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited before רב נחמן בר יצחק: One places the piece inside the whole loaf, breaks, and blesses. He asked: What is your name? He said: שלמן. He said: You are peace, and your teaching is complete, for you made peace between the students.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רב נחמן's practice. He warmly praises the תנא who recited it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the compromise is not just personal piety. A ברייתא actually teaches it. The pun plays on the words שלום (peace) and שלמה (whole or complete): the teaching 'makes peace' between the two sides of the dispute.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: A tanna recited before Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak:
One places the piece inside the whole loaf
and breaks and blesses.
He said to him: What is your name?
He said to him: Shalman.
He said to him: You are peace,
and your teaching is complete,
phrases.notes: A play on words: שלמן, שלום, and שלמה.

phrases.english: for you made peace among the students.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 12's practice with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of placing the piece inside the whole loaf.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recited before רב נחמן בר יצחק.

steps.title: On פסח everyone agrees to use the piece with the whole
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that on פסח everyone agrees to place the piece inside the whole מצה and break, because the פסוק calls מצה 'bread of affliction'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that on פסח one places the piece inside the whole and breaks. Why? Because 'bread of affliction' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a special case. On פסח, nobody argues: you use both the piece and the whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לחם עני means bread of a poor person, and a poor person usually eats broken pieces. So on פסח the broken מצה has its own special importance. That is why the piece is used together with the whole even according to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread of affliction, or bread of the poor (דברים ט״ז:ג)

steps.whatToRemember: Normally, a ירא שמים holds the piece with the whole to satisfy both views. On פסח, everyone does this, because מצה is 'poor man's bread', which is broken bread.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for breaking the middle מצה at the סדר and blessing with a broken מצה together with a whole one.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees on Passover
that one places a piece inside a whole one and breaks.
What is the reason?
"Bread of affliction" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the piece-inside-whole practice to פסח, where it applies according to everyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח, everyone agrees to place the piece inside the whole מצה and break, based on לחם עני.

steps.title: On שבת one must break bread over two loaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that on שבת a person must make המוציא over two whole loaves. The source is the פסוק about the מן, which calls it 'לחם משנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: On שבת a person must make the בְּרָכָה and break bread over two loaves. Why? Because the פסוק says 'לחם משנה', double bread.
steps.whatsHappening: After the discussion of breaking bread on פסח, the גמרא brings a new rule from רבי אבא about breaking bread on שבת. It also gives his source right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שבת, a double portion of מן fell in the מדבר. The תורה calls it 'לחם משנה'. To remember this, every שבת meal begins with two whole loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Double bread. The double portion of מן that fell on ערב שבת.
To break or cut the bread after making המוציא.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of making המוציא over two חלות at every שבת meal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
And on Shabbat a person is obligated
to break bread over two loaves.
What is the reason?
'Double bread' is written.
phrases.notes: שמות ט״ז:כ״ב, about the double portion of מן before שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא וּבְשַׁבָּת חַיָּיב אָדָם לִבְצוֹעַ עַל שְׁתֵּי כִכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the special rule for breaking מצה on פסח to the special rule for breaking bread on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one must make המוציא over two whole loaves, based on 'לחם משנה'.

steps.title: How the אמוראים actually broke the two loaves
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports two practices. רב כהנא held both loaves but cut only one. רבי זירא cut off a piece large enough for his whole meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw רב כהנא hold two loaves and cut only one. רבי זירא would cut off a piece big enough to eat for the entire meal.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know you need two loaves, the גמרא shows how the חכמים actually did it, through what רב אשי saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא shows that you only have to hold both loaves for לחם משנה. You do not have to cut both. רבי זירא adds a way to honor the meal: he cut a very large piece.
steps.confusionAlert: Holding two loaves and cutting two loaves are different things. רב כהנא held two but cut only one.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I saw Rav Kahana
who would take two and break one.
Rabbi Zeira would break off a piece
for the entire meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to carry out רבי אבא's rule of two loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You hold two loaves but cut one. A large piece may be cut for the whole meal.

steps.title: רבינא asks: doesn't a huge piece look greedy?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבי זירא's practice. Cutting such a big piece looks like gluttony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But this looks like gluttony!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא questions the practice of רבי זירא from the last step. Cutting off a giant piece of bread seems to make a person look greedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person should not act in a way that looks like overeating. רבינא's challenge is that רבי זירא's big piece seems to break that rule of proper behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: It looks like, it appears as.
But isn't it...? This opens a challenge.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But it looks like gluttony!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's practice reported in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's practice of cutting a piece for the whole meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting such a huge piece looks like greedy eating, which is improper.

steps.title: It doesn't look greedy because he only does it on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that people see he does not do this on weekdays. So on שבת it clearly shows honor for שבת, not greed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Since he does not do this every day, and today he does, it does not look like gluttony.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's challenge and defends רבי זירא's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greed would show up every day. Since he only cuts a big piece on שבת, people understand that he is honoring the שבת meal. So the act itself does not look greedy.

keyTerms.meaning: Every day, meaning on regular weekdays.

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת: hold two loaves, cut one, and a big piece is fine because it honors שבת.

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּכָל יוֹמָא לָא קָעָבֵיד הָכִי,
phrases.english: Since every other day he does not do so,
and today he does,
it does not look like gluttony.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּכָל יוֹמָא לָא קָעָבֵיד הָכִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual reframing: the special day changes how the act is seen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A large piece always looks greedy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is done only on שבת, it is seen as honoring שבת, not as greed.

steps.title: Making המוציא on the עירוב bread
steps.stepSummary: When רב אמי and רב אסי had the bread of the עירוב, they made המוציא on it at the שבת meal. Their reason was that since one מצוה was already done with it, they wanted to do another מצוה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the bread of the עירוב came into the hands of רב אמי and רב אסי, they would make 'המוציא לחם מן הארץ' on it. They said: Since one מצוה was done with it, let us do another מצוה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new practice about bread on שבת. These חכמים used the עירוב bread as the bread for המוציא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב bread was already used for the מצוה of עירוב, which allows carrying or walking on שבת. They liked to use the same object for a second מצוה, the שבת meal and its המוציא. This teaches that an object used for one מצוה should be valued and used again for another.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to come to them.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of using the עירוב bread, such as the עירוב תבשילין or עירוב חצרות bread, for המוציא at a שבת meal.

phrases.english: Rav Ami and Rav Asi,
when it would happen to them to have
the bread of the eiruv,
would recite over it
'Who brings forth bread from the earth.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: הוֹאִיל וְאִתְעֲבִיד בֵּיהּ מִצְוָה חֲדָא,
phrases.english: They said: Since one מצוה was done with it,
let us do another מצוה with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי כִּי הֲוָה מִתְרְמֵי לְהוּ רִיפְתָּא דְעֵרוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of bread at the שבת meal with a new practice about which bread to use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עירוב bread is used for המוציא on שבת, because an object used for one מצוה should be used for another.
